skill.name: entity-optimizer
skill.description: Use when optimizing a brand, person, organization, or product entity for Knowledge Graph, Wikidata, sameAs, and AI recognition signals. It audits entity evidence, creates a canonical profile, and hands off page-level SEO or GEO work to related skills.
skill.summary: Builds canonical entity profiles and action plans for Knowledge Graph and AI recognition.

content.value_statement: Brands and people can be hard for search engines and AI systems to identify correctly. This skill audits entity signals and creates a practical plan for Knowledge Graph, Wikidata, sameAs, and AI recognition improvements.
actual_capabilities: Audits entity presence across Knowledge Graph, Wikidata, Wikipedia, schema, third-party profiles, and AI recognition signals.
Scores six entity signal categories as pass, partial, or fail with evidence-based next actions.
Creates a canonical entity profile with name, type, domain, sameAs links, identifiers, claims, and disambiguation notes.
Builds a top-priority action plan for structured data, Wikidata, authoritative mentions, and AI-specific entity clarity.
Produces handoff guidance for related SEO and GEO skills when markup, content, or citation work is needed.
limitations: It cannot verify live Knowledge Graph, AI answer, or search results without user-provided data or external tools.
It does not create Wikipedia or Wikidata entries automatically.
It provides entity optimization guidance, not legal advice for privacy or publicity rights.
It is not a page-level content optimizer; related skills handle article drafting and schema implementation.

use_cases.title: Clarify a Brand Entity
use_cases.description: Audit whether Google, Wikidata, directories, schema, and AI tools describe a brand consistently.

use_cases.title: Build Founder Recognition
use_cases.description: Create a sourced profile plan for a public person while checking consent and privacy requirements first.

use_cases.title: Fix Entity Confusion
use_cases.description: Find name collisions, weak sameAs links, and missing qualifiers that cause AI systems to confuse similar entities.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Entity Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with one brand or person and basic facts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit entity presence for [entity name]. The entity type is [brand, person, organization, product, or event], and the primary domain is [domain].

prompt_templates.title: Signal Gap Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you have profiles and existing structured data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review entity signals for [entity name] using these sources: [website], [social profiles], [Wikidata or Wikipedia], and [directory listings]. Identify pass, partial, and fail items.

prompt_templates.title: Disambiguation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when search or AI systems confuse two entities.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a disambiguation plan for [entity name], which is confused with [other entity]. Include naming qualifiers, sameAs fixes, schema changes, and priority evidence sources.

prompt_templates.title: Canonical Profile Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after evidence has been gathered.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a canonical entity profile for [entity name] from these verified facts and sources: [facts and URLs]. Include confidence levels, unresolved conflicts, and the next best skill handoff.

output_examples.input: Audit entity presence for Acme Analytics, a B2B SaaS company.
output_examples.output: The report identifies partial AI recognition, missing Wikidata presence, incomplete sameAs links, and a top action plan for structured data, profile cleanup, and independent citations.

output_examples.input: AI systems confuse our founder with another person of the same name.
output_examples.output: The output recommends stronger qualifiers, a clear author profile, unique sameAs links, source-backed biography facts, and a privacy check before saving a person profile.

output_examples.input: Prepare a canonical entity profile for a product before GEO content work.
output_examples.output: The profile summarizes the product name, type, official domain, identifiers, source-backed claims, topic associations, and open loops for downstream schema and content tasks.

best_practices: Provide official URLs, known profiles, entity type, target topics, and known confusion cases before the audit begins.
Use dated, source-backed claims for every factual statement that may change over time.
Run the recommended AI recognition tests before and after major entity signal changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to create promotional or weakly sourced Wikipedia content.
Do not save a person profile without confirming a lawful basis when privacy rules may apply.
Do not treat AI recognition observations as authority scores without supporting source evidence.

faq.question: What does this skill optimize?
faq.answer: It optimizes entity identity signals for brands, people, organizations, products, works, and events.

faq.question: Does it perform live web searches?
faq.answer: Only when the host provides tools or the user supplies results. Otherwise, it marks live checks as user-to-run.

faq.question: Can it create a Wikidata page for me?
faq.answer: No. It can assess readiness and recommend sourced fields, but it does not publish external entries.

faq.question: How is this different from content optimization?
faq.answer: It defines the entity and its evidence. Related content skills improve pages, articles, and schema implementation.

faq.question: Can it handle personal entities?
faq.answer: Yes, but it asks for privacy and consent checks before saving a canonical profile for a person.

faq.question: What should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the entity name, type, primary domain, official profiles, target topics, and known confusion issues.
